questions.question: The inside rearview mirror is used to:

options.text: See potential hazards on the road.
See vehicles trying to switch lanes.

questions.explanation: The inside rearview mirror in a school bus lets you watch what students are doing inside the bus.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stop, the driver should:

options.text: Talk to students on the bus.

questions.explanation: Always approach bus stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: When taking the driving test and asked to make a turn, you should:

options.text: Not use a turn signal since you were told to make the turn.
Check traffic only to your right.

questions.explanation: When making a turn during the driving test, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: For a basic vehicle control skills test, you are expected to be able to:

options.text: Weave between a line of cones.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test includes backing straight, offset parking, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: When operating a school bus, mirrors should be adjusted:
questions.explanation: Always adjust and check each mirror before you start operating the bus.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Drive straight into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test includes backing straight, offset parking, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: During the driving test, when encountering a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if the other vehicle is going too slow.
Get out of the vehicle to check for a train.
Not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: When students board a bus, they should:

options.text: Sit in the back row first.
Sit in the back row only after all other seats are filled.
Be seated as far from the driver as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit in the back row only after all other seats are filled.
questions.explanation: Students should not sit in the back row unless the bus is full. Sitting closer to the front is safer in a rear-end crash. Students with special needs should sit near the driver.

questions.question: When a school bus is approaching a bus stop, the driver should:
questions.explanation: Approach bus stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: At a passive railroad crossing, the decision to proceed:

options.text: Is indicated by a control device.
Is decided by the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: A passive crossing has no traffic control devices. The driver decides whether it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: If a tornado is approaching and there is no nearby shelter, where should students go?
questions.explanation: If there is no shelter building available, take students to a nearby ditch or culvert. Avoid areas where water could flood. Stay far enough from the bus so it will not fall on you if it tips over.

questions.question: When exiting a bus, a driver must:

options.text: Never make contact with the handrail.

questions.explanation: Face the vehicle and keep three points of contact with the handrail at all times when exiting. Not exiting correctly will result in automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: If students on the bus cause a disturbance while other students are unloading, what should you do?

options.text: Immediately walk to the back of the bus and take care of the disturbance while students unload.
Wait until the students are done unloading and then take care of the disturbance.
Have a student who is closer to the disturbance handle the situation while you supervise unloading.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the students are done unloading and then take care of the disturbance.
questions.explanation: Focus completely on loading or unloading students. Wait until all students have safely exited before handling any behavioral problems.

questions.question: When stopping to pick up students, park at least 10 feet away from them because:

options.text: You will have a good view of their movements.
It will be difficult to get any closer to the students.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have a good view of their movements.
questions.explanation: Park with the front bumper at least 10 feet from students. This makes students walk to the bus and lets you watch them safely.

questions.question: When loading or unloading passengers, a school bus should be placed in ____ if there is no park shift point available.
questions.explanation: Park the bus when loading or unloading. If park is not available, put the bus in neutral and set the parking brake.

questions.question: As a general rule, where should students be kept during an emergency?

options.text: On the side of the road near the bus
In a field away from the bus

questions.explanation: Students are usually safer and easier to control on the bus during an emergency. Only evacuate them if staying on the bus puts them at risk.

questions.question: Before a trip, you should make sure that:

options.text: The grooved pedal surface has not been smoothed out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The grooved pedal surface has not been smoothed out.
questions.explanation: Check that nothing is blocking the pedals. Make sure pedals work correctly and have grooved surfaces for safe use.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:

options.text: How quickly you arrive to your destination.

questions.explanation: The examiner scores you on specific driving maneuvers and your overall driving behavior.

questions.question: A passive railroad crossing:

options.text: Does not have any control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not have any control devices.
questions.explanation: A passive crossing has no traffic control devices. The driver decides whether to cross the tracks.

questions.question: When dropping off students at a school, a driver should:

options.text: Secure the bus by turning off the engine.
Leave the key in the ignition, if leaving the driver's compartment.
Read a book while students unload.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the bus by turning off the engine.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine to secure the bus. Remove the key from the ignition if you leave the driver's area. Always supervise students while they unload.
